RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the July 27, 2006/Sravana 5, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; External Affairs; Housing and Urban Poverty
Alleviation; Information and Broadcasting; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Panchayati Raj; Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances
and Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways;
Space; Statistics and Programme Implementation; Urban
Development; Youth Affairs and Sports )
Total number of questions —20
Safeguard agreement with IAEA
*61. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the draft Bill on the US and
India Nuclear Cooperation Promotion Act
of 2006 states that the US President must
first determine that India and the
International Atomic Energy Agency
(IAEA) have concluded safeguards
agreements requiring the application of
IAEA safeguards in perpetuity; and
(b) if so, the reaction of Government on
this which runs completely contrary to the
assurance given by the Prime Minister in
both Houses of Parliament that India would
approach the IAEA for safeguards only after
USA endorses the July 18, 2005 nuclear
deal?
Sports infrastructure in rural areas
*62. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND
SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is acute
shortage of sports infrastructure facilities
in rural areas;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps taken to start an effective programme
for youth of rural areas; and
(c) the details of the schemes under
which financial assistance is provided for
the promotion of sports in the country
through NGOs and performance review of
such schemes, particularly in Maharashtra
State?

20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Consultative Committees
†*63. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is compulsory to
constitute ‘Consultative Committees’ for
all Ministries;
(b) if so, the names of Ministries under
the present Government functioning since
May, 2004 where ‘Consultative
Committees’ have not been constituted so
far and the reasons therefor; and
(c)  by when the Committees are likely
to be constituted?
Placing of India on “Watch List” by US
*64. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Annual
Report 2006 of the States Department of
the United States has categorized India as
the source, destination, and transit country
for men, women and children trafficked for
the purposes of forced or bonded labour
and commercial sexual exploitation and
have placed our country in the “Watch List”;
(b) if so, the details of Government’s
response, if any, conveyed to the US thereto;
(c)  the basis of the said response; and
(d) the implications of a country being
placed in the “Watch List” by the US
administration?
Stricter Visa regulations in developed
Countries
*65. SHRI SHANTARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Visa regulations in
developed countries have been made
stricter in recent times;
(b) whether the development has
affected Indians proposing to visit these
countries on different types of Visas;
(c)  if so, whether Government have
made any representation with the
Government of these countries in this
regard; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Corporatisation of major ports
*66. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to corporatise all the major ports in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c)  whether a foreign consultancy firm
has been engaged to advise Government in
this regard; and
(d) if so, what are its findings and
recommendations and the targeted date for
finalizing the issue?
Role of Gram Sabhas
*67. KUMARI NIRMALA
DESHPANDE: Will the Minister of
PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:
(a) the role of the Gram Sabhas in
implementing various schemes for helping
the poor;
(b) whether it is a fact that Gram Sabhas
are being neglected and not encouraged to
function; and

21
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c)  if so, the remedial measures planned
to make the Gram Sabhas effective?
Requests for Kuwait war compensation
*68. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) the details of requests for the Kuwait
war compensation from the large number
of people from Kerala;
(b) whether Government have requested
to the United Nations Compensation
Commission to extend the prescribed time
limit for the submission of applications;
and
(c)  if so, the details thereof?
Committee for unbundling of copper
cables
*69. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a Committee has been set
up for unbundling of copper cables of
BSNL/MTNL;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c)  the terms of reference of the
Committee alongwith the names of
Members thereof?
Violation of TRAI guidelines
*70. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that some service providers, are not
following required norms, laid by TRAI,
regarding proof of address of the subscriber;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that in
Haryana and Delhi circles, some complaints
of violation of the TRAI guidelines of
address proof have been registered;
(c)  whether 2000 connections were
issued illegally in this manner by almost all
the service providers;
(d) if so, whether it is not a breach of
national security; and
(e) what steps have been taken by
Government?
Screening of Indian films in Pakistan
*71. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Pakistan has
banned the transmission of some Indian
T.V. channels in that country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c)  whether Pakistan has allowed the
screening of some of the Indian feature films
in their country; and
(d) if so, the names of such films and
the terms and conditions imposed by
Pakistan for screening these Indian films?
Road accidents
†*72. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the number of road accidents
on National and State Highways has

22
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
increased and whether these accidents
usually happen due to trucks;
(b) whether generally those truck
drivers who drive the trucks after consuming
alcohol and drive throughout the night are
responsible for it;
(c)  whether due to the absence of any
stringent law in this regard, drivers commit
such negligence;
(d) whether Government intend to bring
a bill to make more stringent law to check
these accidents; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Dual citizenship
†*73. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of representations
received by the Central Government till
date with respect to giving dual citizenship;
(b) the number of citizens who have
been given dual citizenship, till date;
(c)  the number of persons whose
representations for dual citizenship are
pending and the date from which they are
pending; and
(d) by when these representations
would be disposed off and what are the
reasons for delay in this behalf?
Preparations for Commonwealth Games
†*74. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
 Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of preparations being made
for Commonwealth Games to be held in 2010;
(b) the total number of schemes chalked
out by Government of NCT of Delhi and
other State Governments for conducting
Commonwealth Games; and
(c)  whether the scheme has been
formulated to ensure that tourists visiting
India as well as local residents do not face
any problem during Commonwealth
Games?
Change in method of fixing royalty
given to State Governments
†*75. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in order to
fix the royalty given to the State
Governments in respect of coal production,
change in the existing method is being
contemplated;
(b) if so, the details of the proposed
method and whether it is also a fact that by
adopting the proposed method costs of the
products are bound to rise; and
(c)  if so, Government’s reaction thereto
and the estimated price rise due to adoption
of the proposed method?
Indo-American nuclear pact
†*76. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Indo-American
Nuclear Pact arrived at on 18th July, 2005
has not yet got the approval of American
Senate;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;

23
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c)  whether efforts to add fresh
conditions to the agreements are being made;
and
(d) the reasons for Government’s
acceptance of categorisation and inspection
of military and civilian nuclear
establishments alongwith the criteria
therefor?
Action against National TV channels
†*77. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that the so called National TV
channels telecast obscene scenes repeatedly
in the name of news in order to enhance
Television Rating Programme (TRP);
(b) if so, whether in order to check it,
Government would constitute any
commission which can take stringent action
against such TV channels; and
(c)  the action taken by the Press Council
of India against these channels during the
last five years?
Political solution for Sri Lanka
*78. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Foreign Secretary
visited Sri Lanka and handed over a letter
from Prime Minister to the President of Sri
Lanka and reiterated India’s support for a
political solution;
(b) if so, whether India has been pushing
the Government of Sri Lanka to come out
with a solution devolution package
acceptable to all sections of society,
particularly the Tamils;
(c)  if so, what was the outcome of the
discussions; and
(d) to what extent Sri Lanka has
responded to India’s proposal?
Sale of surplus coal by captive coal
producers
*79. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are planning to permit sale of surplus coal
by captive coal producers to other end-
users;
(b) if so, by when the law would be
enacted; and
(c)  the number of captive coal producers
in India and quantity of their production?
Development of ports in Kerala
*80. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the relevant features of the National
Maritime Development Programme and to
what extent this programme has been
implemented in the country;
(b) whether Government have
proposed the ports of Azhikkal and
Vizhinjam in Kerala among the ports
selected for this programme;

24
(c)  the other ports included in this
programme;
(d) whether the State Government of
Kerala have submitted an outline project
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 21st July, 2006 Secretary-General.
Asadha 30, 1928 (Saka)
for the development of these two ports;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof and whether
the proposal of Kerala has been accepted
by the Central Government?

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the July 27, 2006/Sravana 5, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; External Affairs; Housing and Urban Poverty
Alleviation; Information and Broadcasting; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Panchayati Raj; Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public
Grievances and Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road
Transport and Highways; Space; Statistics and
Programme Implementation; Urban
Development; Youth Affairs
and Sports)
Total number of questions — 143
Setting up of new nuclear plants
256. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up
more nuclear plants following Indo-U.S.
deal;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Nuclear plants in West Bengal and
Orissa
257. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to locate a
nuclear plant in West Bengal;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the norms that have been laid down
for setting up such plants in the country;
(d) whether such a plant is also
proposed to be located in the backward
State of Orissa; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Uranium plants in Maharashtra and
Chhattisgarh
258. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to set up a Uranium processing
plant in Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh; and
(b) if so, by when it is likely to be set
up?
Addition to nuclear energy capacity
259. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Planning

62
Commission has accepted a
recommendation to raise India's nuclear
energy capacity to 1,00,000 MW in 25
years; and
(b) if so, the details of the proposal?
Additional generation of electricity
260. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the annual generation of electricity
by each Nuclear Power Plant during the
last three years, year-wise and plant-wise;
(b) the expected additional generation
of electricity from each plant during the
period 2006-07 and 2007-08; and
(c) the extent to which the demand of
the country shall be met as a result of such
generation of electricity particularly in Uttar
Pradesh?
Opening up of coal sector to private
sector investments
261. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are taking measures to remove the control
that the CIL is enjoying with regard to
supply of coal to domestic consumers;
(b) if so, whether it is a part of the
move in view of Government's decision to
amend the Coal (Nationalization) Act, to
open up coal sector to private sector
investments;
(c) the total number of coal blocks in
the country with CIL and the production
of coal in these blocks during the last 5
years, year-wise and State-wise; and
(d) the reasons for (a) above and
whether any political consensus have been
arrived at with regard to (b) above?
Production and supply of coal
262. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) the present stage of production and
supply of coal by Coal India Ltd. during
the last three years;
(b) whether CIL has developed any new
mining areas to increase coal production
during the above-mentioned period; and
(c) if so, the plans of CIL to increase
production in order to meet the
requirements of industries for power
generation?
Monopoly in coal supply
263. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have initiated
the process of loosening Coal India
Limited's virtual monopoly in supplying
coal to domestic consumers and also
allowed a slew of State Government owned
companies to not only undertake coal
mining in some blocks but also allow them
to sell to non-captive consumers;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when the proposal is likely to be
implemented?
Tribal land taken for coal excavation
in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh
264. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the number of acres of tribal land
that have been taken by his Ministry for

63
coal excavation in Jharkhand and
Chhattisgarh, district-wise, block-wise,
panchayat-wise, during the last five years;
(b) the details of the rehabilitation
package that is offered to the tribals who
are affected and displaced by coal mining
in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh; and
(c) whether the coal companies give
displaced tribals employment, if so, how
many have been given employment and if
not, the plan to compensate them?
Plan for denationalisation of coal
mining blocks
265. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have any plans
to dereserve or denationalise coal mining
blocks for the private sector;
(b) whether Government propose to
bring forward any legislation to
denationalise the coal sector indicating at
what stage the proposal is lying;
(c) whether the draft bill is likely to be
introduced by Government during the
Monsoon Session of Parliament; and
(d) if not, the policy of UPA
Government in regard to coalfields?
Coal mines under the private sector
266. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) the number of coal mines under the
private sector location-wise and the
company-wise;
(b) whether certain private companies
are engaged in illegal mining in the coal mine
area;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the norms laid down for regulating
the coal mining by the private companies;
and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
check the violation of norms by the private
companies?
Black marketing of coal due to
shortage
267. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that because of
less production of coal than that of the
demand its black marketing has taken place;
(b) the total coal production and
consumption during the last three years
from 2003-04 to 2005-06 in the country;
(c) the road map to meet increasing
demand of coal as a source of energy with
having only 9.3 per cent of world coal
reserves in the country; and
(d) whether it is a fact that imported
coal is cheaper than that of our coal and the
countries from which coal is imported?
Committee's recommendations for
import of coal
268. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Committee, headed by T.L. Shankar, set
up to recommend measures to meet the
demand-supply gap and also to examine
the current policy on captive coal mines
etc. has, in the first part of its recent report,
highlighted, inter-alia, that the country will
face pronounced coal shortages over the
next four years and recommended import
of high grade thermal coal; and

64
(b) if so, the details of other major
recommendations/observations made by
the Committee and the action taken/
proposed to be taken thereon?
Business Post Centres
269. SHRI C.
RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether some of the post offices in
the country have started functioning as
Business Post Centres;
(b) if so, the details of locations thereof,
State-wise particularly in Andhra Pradesh;
(c) the main functions of such Centres
and the volume of transactions being made
by them;
(d) whether Government have any
proposal to set up more such Centres in
various parts of the country;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
E-Governance Projects
270. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that recently a
detailed plan has been launched for
execution of 26 mission mode E-governance
projects and eight support components at
an estimated cost of Rs. 23000 crores for
creating citizens-centric and business-
centric environment for governance;
(b) if so, the details thereof, including
the phased programme drawn up for its
execution; and
(c) the details of the monitoring
machinery set up to ensure time-bound
implementation of the various projects so
that the benefits of information technology
are available to the citizens as early as
possible?
Revenue loss to postal department
271. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether after coming down heavily
on telecom operators carrying grey
international long distance telephone calls,
his Ministry has now started to crack down
on courier companies who are allegedly
bringing post from foreign countries into
the country illegally;
(b) if so, whether a number of courier
companies in the country were bringing in
huge consignments of post from foreign
countries and then injecting into the Indian
postal network to avoid payment of
terminal dues to postal department; and
(c) if so, the total revenue loss
Government suffered and the steps taken
to check this revenue loss?
Banking facility in Post Offices
272. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether India Post plans to
introduce anywhere anytime banking
facility and bring all retail services offered
by post offices under one roof;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when the proposal would be
implemented throughout the country?

65
Telephone exchanges in Andhra
Pradesh
273. SHRI C.
RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of telephone
exchanges functioning in Andhra Pradesh
particularly in Cuddapah district and their
exchange-wise capacity as on date;
(b) whether Government propose to
increase the present capacity of the existing
telephone exchanges and also to open some
new telephone exchanges;
(c) if so, the details of the same; and
(d) the steps taken/proposed to be taken
to exhaust the waiting list in the said district?
Redefining of Adjusted Gross Revenue
274. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the telecom companies have
been demanding slashing of fees they will
have to pay to Government and redefining
Adjusted Gross Revenue (AGR);
(b) if so, Government’s reaction in this
regard;
(c) whether the telecom companies are
charging consumers this fees which they
are paying to Government;
(d) if so, whether Government propose
to redefine AGR, so that the benefits are
passed on to the consumers; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Skilled manpower for IT sector
275. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether keeping in view the
impressive growth of the Information
Technology (IT) Sector and the potential
demand for a large work force, there is
enough skilled manpower to match such
demand;
(b) the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the country
which churns out 15 lakh graduates every
year is not in a position to meet with the
needs of the booming I.T. Sector;
(d) whether leading IT Companies in
the country are searching abroad for such
expertise; and
(e) the need for reservation and blocking
of seats in Institutes of higher learning?
Order Book position of ITI
276. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the financial result of ITI during the
last three years including 2005-06;
(b) the steps taken to improve its
turnover and profits;
(c) whether Government had reserved
for ITI 30 per cent of the orders for Rs. 6
crore GSM lines requirement of BSNL;
(d) whether the same reservation has
been put in abeyance since May this year;
(e) if so, the reasons therefor; and

66
(f) if not, the order book position of ITI
vis-a-vis GSM and CDMA equipments?
Revival of Hindustan
 Teleprinters Ltd.
277. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the revival status of Hindustan
Teleprinters Ltd.;
(b) whether the company was referred
to BIFR after the same was privatized; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Service tax on postal services
278. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to levy service tax on postal services;
(b) whether it is not a fact that this
has already been implemented on all
types of postal services including money
orders, postal life insurance, speed post
etc.;
(c) if so, whether Government are aware
that crores of families in India are surviving
on remittances sent by working people
through money orders; and
(d) if so, the justification for imposing
further burden on the lower middle class
families who are struggling to make both
ends meet?
Introduction of differential
security
279. SHRIMATI SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have recently turned down a proposal of
Telecom Department to introduce
differential security related treatment of
Telecom Service Provider based on levels
of Foreign Direct Ownership in individual
companies;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the action Government propose to
take in this matter?
Cheap and quality service to the
subscribers
280. SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the Cellular and WLL service
providers in the country;
(b) whether the WLL telephone service
is not working properly in several parts of
the country;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to ensure cheap and quality
service to the subscribers?

67
